items.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks
items.summary: PseuDRAGON uses knowledge‑guided local LLMs to consistently pseudonymize financial data by storing confirmed judgments and applying exact‑name lookups and learned rules.
items.whyItMatters: It improves data privacy accuracy and auditability for finance teams using local AI models.

items.title: AutoClip-DPZO: Practical Private Clipping Selection for Differentially Private Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
items.summary: AutoClip-DPZO introduces a practical method for selecting the clipping threshold in differentially private zeroth-order LLM fine‑tuning, improving privacy‑utility trade‑offs.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it enhances memory‑efficient, privacy‑preserving fine‑tuning of large language models.

items.title: RepoClean: Evaluating Coding Agents on Repository-Level Obsolete Code Cleanup
items.summary: RepoClean evaluates how LLM agents can detect and safely remove obsolete code from entire repositories.
items.whyItMatters: It helps reduce maintenance costs and prevent bugs in evolving codebases.

items.title: Toward a Theoretical Understanding of Transformer Attention: Bayesian Estimation and Predictive Sufficiency
items.summary: The paper provides a theoretical framework linking Transformer attention to Bayesian posterior estimation and conditions for accurate next-token prediction.
items.whyItMatters: It clarifies when attention truly captures probabilistic inference, guiding more principled model design.

items.title: FMSNO: Scaling Surface Neural Operators by Learned Flow Matching Reparametrisation
items.summary: FMSNO learns a shared mapping from irregular surface meshes to a regular spherical grid, then trains a neural operator on that grid to accelerate inference.
items.whyItMatters: It reduces per-geometry mapping cost, speeding up large‑mesh neural operator applications.

items.title: Learning Teacher Output Preferences from Final Responses for Reasoning Distillation
items.summary: The paper proposes a model-agnostic method to reconstruct hidden chain-of-thought traces from final responses of large language models.
items.whyItMatters: It enables broader, easier extraction of reasoning patterns, improving transparency and potential for safer AI deployment.

items.title: MH-RAG-DIVE: Dynamic and Cost-Efficient Multi-Hop RAG Evaluation via Tree-Cached Dialogue Simulation
items.summary: MH‑RAG‑DIVE introduces a dynamic, tree‑cached dialogue simulation for evaluating multi‑hop, multi‑turn Retrieval‑Augmented Generation systems.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a more realistic, cost‑efficient benchmark for improving conversational AI performance.

items.title: When Does Reasoning Help Entity Disambiguation? Small LLMs In-Domain and Under Shift
items.summary: The paper investigates when reasoning capabilities in small LLMs improve entity disambiguation, especially in-domain and under distribution shift.
items.whyItMatters: It informs how to deploy efficient LLMs for knowledge graph tasks without heavy fine‑tuning.

items.title: Verifiable On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: The article discusses how verifiable on‑policy distillation can supplement sparse RLVR rewards by providing dense supervision for language‑model reasoning.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it improves training efficiency and model reliability in reinforcement learning.

items.title: Accuracy Is Not Evidence: Measuring and Training Evidence Dependence in Video Temporal Grounding
items.summary: The paper introduces a method to assess how much video grounding models rely on specific frames by auditing with fixed-answer edits.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it reveals model biases and improves robustness in video understanding.

items.title: HEART: Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer for ECG Representation Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces HEART, a transformer that adaptively refines ECG representations by hierarchically processing heterogeneous cardiac tokens.
items.whyItMatters: It promises more accurate, context-aware ECG analysis for clinicians and AI diagnostics.

items.title: Topology-Prior-Guided Regional Latent Dynamics for Transient Structural Response Prediction
items.summary: The paper introduces TPLD, a surrogate model that uses topology priors and regional latent dynamics to predict complex transient structural responses efficiently.
items.whyItMatters: It offers faster, more accurate simulations for engineers dealing with large, heterogeneous finite element models.

items.title: Uncovering Separable and Composable Skill Mechanisms in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Recent work has sought to localize the internal mechanisms underlying visual reasoning skills in vision-language models. These methods largely overlook separability and composability in both mechanism identification and evaluation. items.title: Temporal Leakage Distorts the TGB Node Affinity Leaderboard: A Point-in-Time Audit
items.summary: Node affinity prediction in the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB) asks how a node's future interactions will be distributed over other nodes. On this task, methods that reuse past ground-truth labels often outperform temporal graph neural networks, and the state of the art builds on them. items.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
items.summary: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. items.title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
items.summary: Trustworthiness is a crucial issue for generative AI, as modern models can produce convincing and confident responses even when their outputs are incomplete, unsupported, or wrong. The frequent absence of ground-truth knowledge or labels complicates verification of generative AI outputs. items.title: Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks
items.summary: Post-training large language models routinely pools reasoning trajectories from diverse teachers or algorithms, yet it remains unclear whether standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can learn such heterogeneous strategies without explicit mode conditioning. items.title: Evaluating Persona Consistency in LLM User Simulators Without External Reference Annotations
items.summary: Standard evaluations assess LLM-simulated personas against an external ground truth, such as community trait annotations, but that reference is unavailable when the persona is inferred only from a short, task-oriented chat. items.title: A New Perspective on ANN-to-SNN Conversion: Hardware-Aligned Multi-Threshold Neuron Dynamics for Neuromorphic Inference
items.summary: By accumulating spikes over multiple timesteps, rate coding approximates the real-valued activations of an ANN, a principle that underpins numerous ANN-to-SNN conversion methods. However, the converted SNNs typically incur loss in accuracy compared to the original ANN. Existing methods either increase a number of timesteps or introduce more complex neuronal dynamics to reduce this accuracy gap…

items.title: DUET: Dual-MDL Unsupervised Entropy-Trie Segmentation for Low-Resource Languages
items.summary: Morphological segmentation, the task of decomposing words into constituent morphemes, becomes particularly challenging under extreme data scarcity, a regime that can arise in language documentation and linguistic reasoning.
